messages:
maya: Quick run of a precision mixbench on titan-33b across APAC (h100x2) and EU (a100x4). Wanted to surface latency/throughput tradeoffs, quality deltas, and which kernel combos looked stable. Posting the high-level table + a tiny raw dump below.

maya: TL;DR:
- mixfast-v3 (FP16 baseline) used as control.
- safe-int8-2 (GPTQ) gave large speedups on H100 but small regressed LM loss (~+0.8% FP8, +3.2% INT8).
- A100 showed smaller INT8 gains, FP8 often slower than opt FP16 kernels on our stack.

maya: Key numbers (seq=256, batch=8, tokens/sec):
```
region,gpu,profile,lat_p50_ms,lat_p95_ms,tokens_per_sec,rel_speed_vs_fp16,delta_lm_pct
APAC,H100x2,mixfast-v3(FP16),38,62,12000,1.00,0.0%
APAC,H100x2,safe-int8-2(INT8),18,40,26000,2.17,+3.2%
APAC,H100x2,fp8-lite(FP8),30,55,15000,1.25,+0.8%
EU,A100x4,mixfast-v3(FP16),52,95,8500,1.00,0.0%
EU,A100x4,safe-int8-2(INT8),40,110,13500,1.59,+2.9%
EU,A100x4,fp8-lite(FP8),56,120,7200,0.85,+1.1%
```

maya: Notes: H100 run used flash-attn-v3 + custom int8 kernels (kernel tag: h100-int8-gptq-v2). A100 used cudnn/legacy kernels w/ fallback to generic GEMM for some FP8 paths.

sam: Nice. p95 looks a bit spiky on EU INT8 (110ms) — what batch size and joiner config?

maya: batch=8 for all runs. joiner config: dynamic_batcher with max_batch_tokens=2048. spikes come from fallback on a subset of layers (we saw kernel mismatch causing extra memcpy).

jia: Did you run accuracy eval on our standard eval set (squad-like + lm-probe)? Any calibration steps for GPTQ?

maya: yes 1k examples from eval harness (same as onboarding). GPTQ used 128-sample calibration, per-channel. Results in table above are post-calibration. lm-probe loss delta shown as pct change vs FP16 baseline.

leo: For capacity planning — if prod traffic is avg seq=300 and 99th concurrency=120, what does that map to in reserved GPU count for APAC H100 pool?

maya: Rough sketch: with safe-int8-2 on H100x2 we get ~2.1x tokens/sec vs FP16. For target concurrency 120 and avg seq=300 => ~36M tokens/sec sustained. One H100x2 pod (our cluster unit) with INT8 gives ~26M tokens/sec (estimate uses measured throughput at seq256 scaled to 300). So need ~2 pods -> reserve 3 for headroom.

anya: Can you attach the raw logs + perf histograms? want to throw them into the perf dashboard.

maya: uploaded -> https://internal.s3/redwood/bench/1901234567/mixbench.tar.gz (contains raw traces, perf hist, kernel traces).

ops-bot: Test run 1901234567 recorded. Artifacts: s3://redwood/bench/1901234567. CI: mixed-precision smoke tests passed.

sam: Any kernel recs for EU a100 to reduce p95?

maya: For A100 we should switch to the "a100-optimized-matmul-v4" kernel for the critical matmuls (patch in PR #4127). Also enable small-block GEMM that prevents fallback for FP8 paths. Early tests cut p95 by ~20%.

jia: Did you see any quality regression in structured outputs (json-tooling tests) or just LM metrics?

maya: Checked both — JSON schema pass rate dropped 0.3% on INT8, within tolerances. LM loss is the biggest signal. We ran a few prompt templates that surface hallucination and saw negligible delta for FP8, slight uptick INT8 on named-entity recall (~+1.5% error).

leo: Cool. Can we make a quick follow-up: schedule a canary rollout to APAC H100 pool with safe-int8-2 behind feature flag and 5% traffic, monitor LM loss / json-pass / p95 for 48h?

maya: yep I'll open the rollout in console and attach canary config. plan: 5% -> 20% -> 100% if metrics stable.

anya: thanks, will add to perf dashboard and compute cost delta estimates.

maya: One more micro-note: FP8 tuning on A100 needs a kernel patch (see PR note). Until that's merged FP8 on A100 is not reliable. FP8 on H100 looks safe.

sam: :thumbsup: great writeup. can you drop the short CSV into the onboarding doc?

maya: done. added to /docs/onboarding/precision-mixbench.md with a short summary and links.

ops-bot: Canary rollout created: rollout-id rlf_2026_190123_01 (target APAC H100 pool, profile=safe-int8-2, percent=5). Monitor alerts configured.

maya: updating thread as we get canary metrics. cheers.
